To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the serum levels of the enzymes creatine kinase (CK) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) are elevated in patients with acute myocardial infarction and that the extent of the elevation is related to the extent of the infarct, as assessed by the area of myocardium at necropsy that is histologically infarcted.
the extent of irreversible myocardial ischemic damage can be estimated during its early evolution from the serum concentrations of creatine phosphokinase and lactate dehydrogenase isozymes.
the serum creatine kinase (CK) activity-time curve is a sensitive and specific indicator of myocardial infarct size.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(1) the development of a quantitative assay for infarct size based on serum biochemical markers, (2) the application of the assay in experimental animals and in patients with acute myocardial infarction and (3) the use of the assay in studies designed to improve myocardial preservation in ischemic states.

(a) the identification of biochemical markers of infarct extent, (b) the development of a quantitative method for assessing infarct size, and (c) the use of these methods in the evaluation of interventions designed to reduce infarct size.
development and validation of a new approach for quantification of myocardial injury in man.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the extent of myocardial infarction can now be quantitated in the individual patient with a reasonable degree of accuracy.

the measurement of biochemical markers is a useful adjunct to the diagnosis and prognosis of patients with myocardial infarction, but that the clinical value of these markers is limited by the lack of specificity of the biochemical changes.
the biochemical markers are not yet ready for clinical use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the biochemical markers for myocardial infarction are useful in the diagnosis, prognosis, and management of patients with acute myocardial infarct.

we have shown that measurement of serum CK-MB activity can predict the extent of infractions and that the measurement of serum CPK isoenzymes can be used as a prognostic tool in patients with acute myocardial infarction.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the measurement of cardiac troponins, in conjunction with other markers of myocardial necrosis, is a reliable method to estimate infarct size.

the extent of irreversible injury in the early phase of myocardial infarction can be estimated by measuring the release of creatine kinase (CK) and its isozyme CK-MB from ischemic myocardium into blood.

the use of biochemical markers of infarction in serum is feasible and that their use in the clinical setting may be of considerable benefit in the assessment of the extent of ischemic injury and in the selection of appropriate therapy.
